question_en: What is the timeline for expedited reporting of fatal or life-threatening unexpected ADRs?
question_es: ¿Cuál es el plazo de notificación expeditiva de una reacción adversa inesperada mortal o potencialmente mortal?
expected_keywords: 7 calendar days|7 días naturales|7 días calendario|siete días naturales|siete días
8 additional calendar days|8 días naturales adicionales|8 días calendario adicionales|8 días adicionales|ocho días adicionales
notes: ICH E2A §III.B.1 (p.7): notify as soon as possible, no later than 7 calendar days after first knowledge; complete report within 8 additional calendar days.
reference: Fatal or life-threatening unexpected ADRs in clinical investigations: regulators are notified as soon as possible but no later than 7 calendar days after the sponsor's first knowledge that a case qualifies, followed by as complete a report as possible within 8 additional calendar days (ICH E2A §III.B.1).

question_en: How many days does the sponsor have to report a serious unexpected ADR that is not fatal or life-threatening?
question_es: ¿Cuántos días tiene el promotor para notificar una reacción adversa grave e inesperada que no sea mortal ni potencialmente mortal?
expected_keywords: 15 calendar days|15 días naturales|15 días calendario|quince días naturales|quince días
notes: ICH E2A §III.B.2 (p.7): as soon as possible but no later than 15 calendar days after first knowledge that the case meets the minimum criteria.
reference: Serious, unexpected ADRs that are not fatal or life-threatening: filed as soon as possible but no later than 15 calendar days after the sponsor's first knowledge that the case meets the minimum criteria for expedited reporting (ICH E2A §III.B.2).

question_en: How does ICH E2A define a serious adverse event or reaction?
question_es: ¿Cómo define ICH E2A un acontecimiento adverso grave?
notes: ICH E2A §II.B (p.5): any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose results in death, is life-threatening, requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalisation, results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity, or is a congenital anomaly/birth defect. Note: 'life-threatening' = at risk of death at the time of the event. All five criteria are required; the definition spans two chunks.
reference: Any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose: results in death; is life-threatening (the patient was at risk of death at the time of the event, not hypothetically); requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalisation; results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity; or is a congenital anomaly/birth defect. Medical and scientific judgement applies to important medical events that may jeopardise the patient or require intervention (ICH E2A §II.B).

question_en: When is an adverse drug reaction considered 'unexpected' under ICH E2A?
question_es: ¿Cuándo se considera 'inesperada' una reacción adversa según ICH E2A?
expected_keywords: not consistent|no es coherente|no es consistente|no concuerda|no se corresponde
Investigator's Brochure|IB|product information|source document|source documents|información del producto|documento de referencia|documentos de referencia
notes: ICH E2A §II.A.3 (p.4): nature or severity not consistent with the applicable product information (e.g. the Investigator's Brochure for an unapproved IMP).
reference: An adverse reaction whose nature or severity is not consistent with the applicable product information (e.g. the Investigator's Brochure for an unapproved investigational product); reports adding significant information on the specificity or severity of a known ADR also count as unexpected (ICH E2A §II.A.3, §III.C).

question_en: What are the minimum criteria a case must meet before an expedited initial report is submitted?
question_es: ¿Qué criterios mínimos debe cumplir un caso para enviar la notificación expeditiva inicial?
expected_keywords: suspect medicinal product|suspect product|medicamento sospechoso|producto sospechoso
identifiable reporting source|fuente notificadora identificable|fuente de notificación identificable
notes: ICH E2A §III.C (p.8): an identifiable patient, a suspect medicinal product, an identifiable reporting source (and an event/outcome identified as serious and unexpected with reasonable suspected causal relationship, p.11).
reference: An initial expedited report is due within the prescribed time as long as the minimum criteria are met: an identifiable patient, a suspect medicinal product, an identifiable reporting source, and an event or outcome that can be identified as serious and unexpected and for which there is a reasonable suspected causal relationship (ICH E2A §III.C and Attachment 1).

question_en: Which elements must the informed consent discussion and form cover according to ICH E6(R3)?
question_es: ¿Qué elementos deben cubrir la discusión y el formulario de consentimiento informado según ICH E6(R3)?
expected_keywords: purpose of the trial|propósito del ensayo|objetivo del ensayo|finalidad del ensayo
notes: ICH E6(R3) §2.8.10 (pp.24-26): list (a)-(v): purpose, research nature, IMP and randomisation probability, procedures, participant responsibilities, foreseeable risks, expected benefits, alternatives, injury compensation, payment, expenses, voluntary participation, data handling and access, contacts, etc. Keywords sample the beginning, middle and end of the list so a truncated answer fails.
reference: ICH E6(R3) §2.8.10 lists items (a)-(v), as applicable, including: the purpose of the trial (a); that it involves research and its experimental aspects (b); the investigational product and probability of random assignment (c); procedures including invasive ones (d); what is expected of participants (e); reasonably foreseeable risks or inconveniences (f); reasonably expected benefits (g); compensation and/or treatment for trial-related injury (i); prorated payment (j); expenses (k); that participation is voluntary and the participant may withdraw at any time without penalty (l); contacts (r); circumstances for termination of participation (s); availability of results (v). A correct answer gives the whole list or says it is giving only part of it.

question_en: What must happen when a participant or their legally acceptable representative cannot read the informed consent form?
question_es: ¿Qué debe ocurrir cuando el participante o su representante legal no sabe leer el formulario de consentimiento informado?
notes: ICH E6(R3) §2.8.9 (p.24): an impartial witness present (remotely or in person) during the entire discussion; form read and explained; oral consent; witness signs. Glossary 'Impartial Witness' (Appendix C.3.3, p.81).
reference: If the participant or the legally acceptable representative cannot read, an impartial witness should be present (remotely or in person) during the entire informed consent discussion; after the consent form and other information are read and explained and the participant or representative has orally consented and, if capable, signed and dated the form, the witness signs and dates it, attesting that the information was accurately explained to and apparently understood by the participant (ICH E6(R3) §2.8.9; glossary 'Impartial Witness').

question_en: What does ICH E6(R3) say about consent in emergency situations where it cannot be obtained before trial participation?
question_es: ¿Qué dice ICH E6(R3) sobre el consentimiento en situaciones de emergencia en las que no puede obtenerse antes de la participación?
expected_keywords: as soon as possible|lo antes posible|tan pronto como sea posible|lo más pronto posible
legally acceptable representative|representante legalmente aceptable|representante legal
notes: ICH E6(R3) Principle 2.4 (p.11): consent obtained from the participant or their legally acceptable representative as soon as possible, in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements and IRB/IEC approval.
reference: In emergency situations where consent cannot be obtained before participation, consent should be obtained from the participant or their legally acceptable representative as soon as possible, in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements and IRB/IEC-approved processes (ICH E6(R3) Principle 2.4); the IRB/IEC must determine that the protocol adequately addresses the ethical concerns of such trials (§1.2.6).

question_en: Under ICH E6(R3), what must the investigator do when a serious adverse event occurs?
question_es: Según ICH E6(R3), ¿qué debe hacer el investigador cuando ocurre un acontecimiento adverso grave?
notes: ICH E6(R3) §2.7.2 (p.22): report all SAEs immediately to the sponsor (after reasonably becoming aware), with an assessment of causality, except those the protocol identifies as not needing immediate reporting; follow-up reports as necessary.
reference: All serious adverse events should be reported immediately (after the investigator reasonably becomes aware) to the sponsor, except those the protocol identifies as not needing immediate reporting; the report includes an assessment of causality; subsequent information is submitted as follow-up reports as necessary; for deaths, additional information requested (e.g. autopsy reports) is supplied (ICH E6(R3) §2.7.2).

question_en: What are the sponsor's obligations regarding SUSARs under ICH E6(R3)?
question_es: ¿Qué obligaciones tiene el promotor respecto a las SUSAR según ICH E6(R3)?
expected_keywords: regulatory authority|regulatory authorities|autoridad reguladora|autoridades reguladoras|autoridad regulatoria|autoridades regulatorias
notes: ICH E6(R3) §3.13.2 (p.43): expedite reporting of all SUSARs to regulatory authorities per applicable requirements and ICH E2A; report SUSARs to investigators/institutions and IRB/IEC in a manner reflecting urgency. IRB/IEC also receives SUSARs (§1.4.8).
reference: The sponsor should expedite the reporting to the regulatory authorities of all suspected, unexpected and serious adverse reactions (SUSARs) in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements and ICH E2A, and report SUSARs to investigators/institutions and IRBs/IECs in a manner that reflects the urgency of action required (ICH E6(R3) §3.13.2); the IRB/IEC should receive SUSARs (§1.4.8).

question_en: What is the Investigator's Brochure and what is its purpose?
question_es: ¿Qué es el manual del investigador (Investigator's Brochure) y para qué sirve?
expected_keywords: investigational product|producto en investigación|producto de investigación|IMP
notes: ICH E6(R3) Appendix A.1 (p.59): a compilation of the clinical and nonclinical data on the IMP relevant to its study in human participants; provides investigators with information to support compliance with the protocol and a risk-benefit assessment. Sponsor keeps it up to date (A.1.1, 3.15.1).
reference: The Investigator's Brochure is a compilation of the clinical and nonclinical data on the investigational product(s) relevant to their study in human participants; its purpose is to provide investigators and others involved in the trial with the information needed to understand and comply with key features of the protocol and to make an unbiased risk-benefit assessment; the sponsor is generally responsible for keeping it up to date (ICH E6(R3) Appendix A.1, A.1.1, §3.15.1).

question_en: For how long and by whom must essential records be retained according to ICH E6(R3)?
question_es: ¿Durante cuánto tiempo y quién debe conservar los documentos esenciales según ICH E6(R3)?
expected_keywords: required period|retention period|período requerido|periodo requerido|período de retención|periodo de retención|período de conservación|periodo de conservación
no longer needed|ya no son necesarios|ya no se necesitan|no longer required
notes: ICH E6(R3) Principle 9.5 (p.13) and §2.12.12 (p.30): retained securely by sponsors and investigators for the required period per applicable regulatory requirements, or until the sponsor informs the investigator they are no longer needed; available to regulators, monitors, auditors, IRB/IEC.
reference: Sponsors and investigators/institutions should retain essential records securely for the required period in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements, or until the sponsor informs the investigator/institution they are no longer needed; the records should remain complete, readable and directly accessible to regulatory authorities, monitors, auditors and IRBs/IECs, and alterations should be traceable (ICH E6(R3) Principle 9.5, §2.12.12, §3.6.3, Appendix C.2.6-C.2.7).

question_en: What does the Declaration of Helsinki say about research with participants who cannot give consent?
question_es: ¿Qué dice la Declaración de Helsinki sobre la investigación con participantes que no pueden dar su consentimiento?
expected_keywords: legally authorized representative|representante legalmente autorizado|representante legal
notes: Helsinki 2024 ¶28-30: consent from the legally authorized representative considering the participant's preferences; only if the research is likely to benefit them personally or entails minimal risk and burden; assent sought when possible, dissent respected (¶29); ¶30 covers research in conditions preventing consent. Reference extended with the verified ¶30 text on 2026-11-08 after the judge marked a correct answer 'incorrect' against the earlier, thinner reference.
reference: For potential participants incapable of giving free and informed consent, the physician or other qualified individual must seek consent from the legally authorized representative, considering the preferences and values expressed by the potential participant; such persons are in situations of particular vulnerability and must only be included if the research is likely to personally benefit them or entails only minimal risk and minimal burden; when they can give assent it must be sought in addition, and their dissent respected (¶28-29). Research with participants physically or mentally incapable of consent (e.g. unconscious patients) may be done only if the condition that prevents consent is a necessary characteristic of the research group; consent is sought from the legally authorized representative; if none is available and the research cannot be delayed, it may proceed without consent provided the specific reasons are stated in the protocol and a research ethics committee has approved it, and consent to remain in the research must be obtained as soon as possible (¶30). (Declaration of Helsinki 2024 ¶28-30.)

question_en: Under what circumstances does the Declaration of Helsinki allow the use of placebo?
question_es: ¿En qué circunstancias permite la Declaración de Helsinki el uso de placebo?
expected_keywords: no proven intervention|no existe una intervención probada|no exista una intervención probada|no existe ninguna intervención probada|no hay una intervención probada
notes: Helsinki 2024 ¶33: benefits/risks of a new intervention tested against the best proven one(s), except where no proven intervention exists, or where compelling and scientifically sound methodological reasons require placebo/no intervention and participants will not be subject to additional risks of serious or irreversible harm.
reference: A new intervention must be tested against the best proven intervention(s), except: where no proven intervention exists, placebo or no intervention is acceptable; or where, for compelling and scientifically sound methodological reasons, an intervention other than the best proven one, placebo or no intervention is necessary to determine efficacy or safety and participants will not be subject to additional risks of serious or irreversible harm. Extreme care must be taken to avoid abuse of this option (Declaration of Helsinki 2024 ¶33).

question_en: What post-trial provisions does the Declaration of Helsinki require?
question_es: ¿Qué disposiciones posteriores al ensayo exige la Declaración de Helsinki?
notes: Helsinki 2024 ¶34: in advance of a clinical trial, sponsors and researchers must arrange post-trial provisions for all participants who still need an intervention identified as beneficial; the protocol must describe them (¶22).
reference: In advance of a clinical trial, sponsors and researchers must arrange post-trial provisions, provided by themselves, healthcare systems or governments, for all participants who still need an intervention identified as beneficial and reasonably safe in the trial; exceptions must be approved by a research ethics committee; specific information on post-trial provisions is disclosed in informed consent, and the protocol must describe them (Declaration of Helsinki 2024 ¶34, ¶22).

question_en: Does the Declaration of Helsinki require trials to be registered?
question_es: ¿Exige la Declaración de Helsinki registrar los ensayos?
expected_keywords: publicly accessible database|base de datos de acceso público|base de datos accesible al público|base de datos públicamente accesible
notes: Helsinki 2024 ¶35: research involving human participants must be registered in a publicly accessible database before recruitment of the first participant.
reference: Medical research involving human participants must be registered in a publicly accessible database before recruitment of the first participant (Declaration of Helsinki 2024 ¶35).

question_en: Compare what ICH E6(R3) and the Declaration of Helsinki require when enrolling participants who are not capable of giving informed consent themselves.
question_es: Compara lo que exigen ICH E6(R3) y la Declaración de Helsinki al incluir participantes que no pueden dar su consentimiento informado por sí mismos.
expected_keywords: legally authorized representative|representante legalmente autorizado|minimal risk|riesgo mínimo
notes: Multi-source: E6(R3) Principle 2.1 (p.11: 'legally acceptable representatives, acting in the participant's best interest, should provide consent'), §2.8.13 (participants informed per understanding) and §2.4 (emergencies) vs Helsinki ¶28-30 (legally authorized representative, benefit or minimal risk, assent/dissent). Both documents must be retrieved and attributed separately. Principle 2.1 was added to the expected sections after reading a correct answer that cited it (2026-11-08).
reference: ICH E6(R3): for potential participants unable to provide informed consent, their legally acceptable representatives, acting in the participant's best interest, should provide consent before participation; the participants should be informed in a manner that facilitates their understanding and, if capable, sign or assent (Principle 2.1, §2.8.13); minors' assent as appropriate. Declaration of Helsinki 2024: consent from the legally authorized representative considering the participant's preferences and values; inclusion only if the research is likely to benefit them personally or entails only minimal risk and burden; assent sought and dissent respected (¶28-30). A correct answer attributes each position to its document.

question_en: What does ICH E6(R3) require when reported trial data are changed or corrected?
question_es: ¿Qué exige ICH E6(R3) cuando se modifican o corrigen datos del ensayo ya registrados?
expected_keywords: audit trail|pista de auditoría|registro de auditoría|rastro de auditoría
notes: ICH E6(R3) §2.12.6 (p.29): changes/corrections traceable, explained if necessary, must not obscure the original entry (audit trail, §2.12.2 p.28). §3.16.1 (p.47-49): sponsor must not change investigator/participant data unless justified and agreed; corrections justified and supported by source records; computerised-system audit trails.
reference: Changes or corrections to reported data should be traceable, explained if necessary, and must not obscure the original entry (audit trail); data reported to the sponsor should be consistent with source records or discrepancies explained (ICH E6(R3) §2.12.6, §2.12.2). The sponsor should not change data entered by investigators or participants unless justified and agreed, and corrections should be justified and supported by source records; computerised systems need audit trails (§3.16.1).

question_en: From the investigator to the regulatory authority: who reports a serious adverse reaction to whom, and within which timelines, according to ICH E6(R3) and ICH E2A?
question_es: Del investigador a la autoridad reguladora: ¿quién notifica una reacción adversa grave a quién y en qué plazos, según ICH E6(R3) e ICH E2A?
expected_keywords: 7 calendar days|7 días naturales|7 días calendario|siete días naturales|siete días
15 calendar days|15 días naturales|15 días calendario|quince días naturales|quince días
notes: Multi-source: investigator -> sponsor immediately with causality (E6(R3) §2.7.2); sponsor -> regulators expedited per E2A (E6(R3) §3.13.2): 7 days fatal/life-threatening + 8 for completion, 15 days other serious unexpected (E2A §III.B); sponsor -> investigators/IRB-IEC with urgency.
reference: Investigator to sponsor: all SAEs immediately, with a causality assessment (ICH E6(R3) §2.7.2). Sponsor to regulatory authorities: expedited reporting of SUSARs in accordance with ICH E2A (E6(R3) §3.13.2): fatal or life-threatening unexpected ADRs no later than 7 calendar days, plus as complete a report as possible within 8 additional days; other serious unexpected ADRs no later than 15 calendar days (ICH E2A §III.B). Sponsor to investigators/institutions and IRBs/IECs with appropriate urgency.
